Ghana’s LGBTQ community is living in fear after the country’s parliament approved a sweeping bill that criminalises the promotion of LGBTQ+ activities and identifying as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer, rights groups have warned.

The east African nation had sued the current UK government for more than £100m, claiming it was owed after a breach of an agreement.

The first shipwrecks linked to the real pirates of the Caribbean in the Bahamas have been discovered by an international team co-directed by a British marine archaeologist.

Riot police fired teargas at teachers who were marching toward Mexico City’s historic Zócalo plaza, just days before the square is expected to host the 2026 World Cup “Fan Fest”. The incident is the second time police have clashed with teachers in the past week, and more conflict is likely as Mexico City prepares to hold the opening game of the Fifa World Cup on 11 June.

guardian.description:
Success of far-right presidential candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella, suggests some voters are ‘fed up with politics’

The far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella and the leftwing senator Iván Cepeda have just under three weeks to compete for the roughly 3.6m votes that did not go to either of them in the first round of Colombia’s presidential election.

That is no insignificant number, given that De la Espriella’s lead over Cepeda amounted to little more than 670,000 votes – 43.

Powerful winds and rain expected in parts of Japan and Australia, while temperatures in Spain could hit 40C

rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans
rfi.description: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.title: France bans Israeli offensive weapons on Europe's largest arms trade show
rfi.description: France has banned the display of Israeli offensive weapons at the 2026 edition of the Eurosatory international defence and security exhibition which opens on 15 June.

rfi.title: WHO seeks more aid for Congo as ebola outbreak continues to spread
rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.title: Mozambique claims five of its nationals killed killed in South Africa 'xenophobic attacks'
rfi.description: Mozambique has claimed that five of its nationals were killed in xenophobic attacks in South Africa at the weekend, as efforts got under way on Tuesday to repatriate hundreds of others.

rfi.title: New York Times chief slams AI companies for 'theft' of intellectual property
rfi.description: The head of The New York Times newspaper launched a scathing attack on artificial intelligence companies, accusing them of "shameless theft of intellectual property" and of threatening journalism. He was speaking at a global media congress on Monday in the southern French city of Marseille.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum
rfi.description: A museum in eastern France has filed a police complaint after a banana forming the centrepiece of Maurizio Cattelan’s multimillion-dollar conceptual artwork "Comedian" was stolen from an exhibition.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Morocco, African champions by ruling
rfi.description: Morocco arrive at the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's highest-ranked side in the Fifa standings. In the second of a nine-part series on African squads at the tournament, RFI profiles a nation making its seventh World Cup appearance.

rfi.title: Gulf states arrested over 1,000 for Iran war social media posts: Amnesty
rfi.description: More than 1,000 people have been arrested across Gulf states for sharing information or opinions related to the Iran-US-Israeli war, in what Amnesty International has described as a “widespread crackdown” on freedom of expression.

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion
rfi.description: Ethiopia holds parliamentary and regional elections on Monday that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party to win by a large margin, despite significant unrest across much of the country.

rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon
rfi.description: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

euronews.title: Massive drug tunnel uncovered beneath US-Mexico border
euronews.description: US authorities released footage of a sophisticated tunnel running beneath the US-Mexico border, saying it was used to smuggle more than $45 million worth of cocaine from Tijuana into California.

euronews.title: Iran World Cup squad to head for Mexico via Spain
euronews.description: Iran’s national football team will travel to Spain before heading to its World Cup base in Mexico, despite players still awaiting Mexican and US visas ahead of the 2026 tournament. The 2026 World Cup is being hosted jointly by the United States, Mexico and Canada.

euronews.title: 'La Caverne du Pont-Neuf' damaged by wind, opening postponed
euronews.description: The temporary artwork failed to withstand Tuesday afternoon's high winds and heavy downpours, and will no longer open to the public on 6 June as planned.

euronews.title: Russia may launch another large scale attack against Ukraine tonight, Zelenskyy warns
euronews.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a stark warning on Tuesday evening saying that according to Ukraine’s intelligence Russia may launch another large-scale aerial attack tonight. It comes as Moscow is exploiting a critical shortage of air defence interceptor missiles.

euronews.title: Health ministry approves new framework statute despite health workers' strike call in Spain
euronews.description: The government says the main trade unions back the reform, despite months of protests by professionals across the political spectrum. The draft law still needs Congress approval.

euronews.title: 'Murcia deploys Military Emergencies Unit to Espuña fire and calls for better coordination'
euronews.description: The fire has led Murcia’s government to put the Military Emergency Unit on alert and raise the Infomur plan to level 2, as regional and central authorities swap messages over the need for coordination.

euronews.title: European Commission is set to criticise Italy for weak industrial strategy
euronews.description: The Commission will criticise Italy’s lack of robust industrial plans and calls for measures to incentivise investment in capital markets as well as reform of tax system, in country-specific recommendations to be published tomorrow.

As incursions multiply across NATO and EU member states, leaders are racing to strengthen defences against a growing threat that blends military pressure, disruption and psychological warfare.

euronews.title: Why is the EU establishing return hubs for migrants — and why are they so controversial?
euronews.description: The new migration law approved on Monday allows EU countries to establish return centres outside the bloc. But critics warn it could lead to human rights violations, while governments are seeking partner countries to host the facilities.

euronews.title: IRGC says Iran has more 'trump cards' up its sleeve as talks hang by a thread
euronews.description: A senior IRGC general said Iran had not revealed all its military capabilities and was ready for direct confrontation with the US and NATO, as hardliners linked to acting IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi were identified as the force behind Monday's suspension of indirect negotiations with Washington.

euronews.description: State Ports' monitoring networks recorded all-time May temperature highs at 18 of their 29 buoys, from Galicia and the Cantabrian coast to the Mediterranean, peaking at 26.58°C off Mahon.

euronews.title: Southern energy corridors set to dominate supplies to Europe, global leaders say
euronews.description: The rapid reshape of global energy supply routes and markets is a key focus at the Baku Energy Week 2026.

euronews.title: France detains tanker linked to Iranian network accused of moving Russian oil
euronews.description: The seizure is the latest evidence of France's efforts to crack down on vessels suspected of helping Russia evade sanctions imposed following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.

euronews.description: Young women who had just turned 18 were lured into creating erotic photos and videos before signing management contracts with the perpetrators, who promised to grow their careers.

euronews.title: A blood test could flag Alzheimer’s risk early. But how reliable is it?
euronews.description: Scientists have developed a blood test that could spot signals of Alzheimer's disease at a much younger age.

euronews.title: €25 million invested, €150 million earned: the 'miraculous' return on the Pope's visit
euronews.description: In what it hails as a loaves-and-fishes miracle, the Spanish Bishops' Conference says Pope Leon XIV’s trip to Spain will bring in five times its cost, though less than the 2011 visit’s 354 million euros.

lemonde.description: « Face à un pouvoir répressif » (3/3). Six ans après la fin du grand mouvement prodémocratie qui a ébranlé le pays, le harcèlement judiciaire est toujours à l’œuvre contre ceux qui continuent à promouvoir la liberté d’expression.

lemonde.title: De Neuilly à la frontière suisse, ces 20 villes où se concentrent les Français aisés
lemonde.description: La commune des Hauts-de-Seine est la ville française qui compte la plus forte proportion de ménages à très hauts revenus, selon une étude de l’Observatoire des inégalités, publiée mardi 2 juin. Le classement est dominé par l’Ouest parisien et les abords de Genève.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky craint une nouvelle frappe massive russe sur l’Ukraine, après les attaques qui ont fait 23 morts la nuit précédente
lemonde.description: « Je vous en prie, soyez attentifs aux sirènes d’alerte aérienne », a insisté le président ukrainien dans une allocution vidéo diffusée mardi soir, se reposant sur des informations des services de renseignement.

lemonde.title: Cancer du sein post-ménopause : les fruits et légumes bio associés à une baisse du risque
lemonde.description: Selon des travaux français, pour chaque portion de 100 grammes de fruits et légumes conventionnels remplacés quotidiennement par leurs équivalents issus de l’agriculture biologique, le risque de développer un cancer du sein post-ménopausique est réduit de 10 %.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump renonce à créer un fonds chargé d’indemniser ses partisans poursuivis sous l’administration Biden
lemonde.description: Une juge fédérale avait provisoirement gelé, vendredi, ce fonds doté de près d’1,8 milliard de dollars. Les démocrates l’avaient qualifié de « caisse noire » destinée notamment aux émeutiers du 6 janvier 2021.

lemonde.title: Crise énergétique : l’Italie obtient un aménagement minimal du pacte de stabilité et de croissance
lemonde.description: Les Etats membres pourront, sous certaines conditions, utiliser jusqu’à 0,3 % de leur produit intérieur brut par an pour aider les entreprises et les ménages à faire face à la flambée des prix de l’énergie.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : le Hezbollah est le « seul obstacle » à la paix entre Israël et le Liban, selon le chef de la diplomatie américaine, Marco Rubio
lemonde.description: « Israël et le Liban pourraient conclure un accord de paix dès demain. Israël n’a aucune revendication territoriale au Liban », a affirmé mardi Marco Rubio, lors d’une audition devant la commission des affaires étrangères du Sénat américain. Il a répété que « sans l’Iran, il n’y aurait pas de Hezbollah ».

lemonde.title: Patrick Poivre d’Arvor visé par deux nouvelles plaintes pour agressions sexuelles
lemonde.description: Treize plaintes avaient déjà été déposées, mais plus de 40 femmes ont témoigné auprès de la justice contre l’ancien présentateur des JT d’Antenne 2 puis de TF1, qui conteste les accusations de viols et d’agressions sexuelles portées contre lui.

lemonde.title: Au Danemark, un troisième mandat pour la première ministre Mette Frederiksen
lemonde.description: Après des tractations historiquement longues, la patronne des sociaux-démocrates danois a réussi à former une coalition de centre gauche, incluant quatre partis, dans le cadre d’un paysage politique éclaté.

lemonde.title: Fin de vie : désaccord confirmé entre députés et sénateurs, vers une adoption définitive le 15 juillet
lemonde.description: Après une nouvelle lecture dans chaque chambre, le gouvernement « donnera le dernier mot aux députés le 15 juillet », a annoncé le ministre des relations avec le Parlement, Laurent Panifous, sur Sud Radio.

lemonde.title: Roland-Garros 2026, les résultats du mardi 2 juin : Alexander Zverev et Jakub Mensik qualifiés pour les demi-finales, la Russe Mirra Andreeva affrontera l’Ukrainienne Marta Kostyuk
lemonde.description: Si l’Allemand a facilement éliminé Rafael Jodar, ce fut plus compliqué pour le Tchèque face à Fonseca. La journée avait commencé par les deux premiers quarts féminins, et notamment la qualification de Marta Kostyuk dans un duel 100 % ukrainien.

lemonde.title: Meurtre d’un étudiant au Royaume-Uni : des manifestants s’en prennent à la police après la diffusion d’une vidéo suscitant l’indignation
lemonde.description: La diffusion d’images montrant la police menotter un étudiant alors qu’il venait d’être poignardé suscite une vive émotion au Royaume-Uni. Mardi soir, des policiers ont été pris pour cible en marge d’une manifestation, à Southampton, au sud de l’Angleterre.

lemonde.title: Santé mentale des jeunes : des souffrances psychiques persistantes, une « évolution contrastée »
lemonde.description: L’agence Santé publique France a communiqué les résultats de deux enquêtes sur la santé mentale des écoliers d’une part, des collégiens et lycéens d’autre part, avec des indicateurs plus défavorables pour les jeunes filles. Le gouvernement promet un « coupe-file » pour les élèves en détresse repérés dans le cadre scolaire, censé leur permettre d’accéder plus rapidement aux soins.

lemonde.title: Célébration du sacre du PSG : deux personnes mortes après avoir chuté dans la Seine, un troisième accident mortel sur le périphérique parisien
lemonde.description: Le parquet de Paris a communiqué un nouveau bilan. Une des victimes est morte mardi des suites de sa noyade dans la Seine dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche.

lemonde.title: Albanie : manifestations contre un projet de complexe touristique attribué au gendre de Donald Trump
lemonde.description: Jared Kushner prévoit de transformer l’île de Sazan – qui abritait autrefois une base militaire communiste secrète – en une destination touristique de luxe, un projet estimé à 1,4 milliard d’euros.

lemonde.title: « C’est la Palme d’or de l’hôtellerie française » : l’Etat donne sa nouvelle liste des 33 palaces les plus luxueux du pays
lemonde.description: La nouvelle promotion du label d’Etat « Palaces de France » a été révélée mardi 2 juin, avec six entrées et quatre sorties. Une manière de valoriser ce secteur vitrine du savoir-faire hexagonal, même si les propriétaires de ces établissements sont rarement français.

france24fr.title: Trump - Netanyahou : je t'aime, moi non plus !
france24fr.description: Selon le média Axios, Donald Trump aurait eu une conversation houleuse avec Benyamin Netanyahou au sujet de la guerre menée par Israël au Liban. Il aurait notamment lâché ces mots : "Putain qu’est-ce que tu fous ? Tu es complètement fou !" Si les deux hommes se connaissent de longue date, leur relation n'a jamais été aussi tendue.

france24fr.title: À Paris, deux morts dans la Seine en marge des célébrations du sacre du PSG
france24fr.description: Selon un nouveau bilan publié mardi, deux personnes ont été retrouvées mortes après être tombées dans la Seine samedi soir en marge des célébrations du sacre du PSG en Ligue des champions.

france24fr.title: Remaniement ministériel au Sénégal : une nouvelle équipe de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes
france24fr.description: Fin du suspense au Sénégal. Après 11 jours d'attente, Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a composé ce lundi, un nouveau gouvernement. Une équipe sans la participation du Pastef, le parti dirigé par son ancien Premier ministre, nouveau président de l'Assemblée nationale et compagnon de route de longue date, Ousmane Sonko. Un gouvernement de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes.

france24fr.title: Pollution au chlordécone aux Antilles : le Parlement reconnaît une responsabilité de l'État
france24fr.description: Le Parlement a adopté, mardi, une proposition de loi visant à reconnaître la "part de responsabilité" de l'État dans le scandale du chlordécone aux Antilles, malgré une ambition amoindrie en cours d'examen au Sénat.

france24fr.title: Une proposition de loi pour limiter l'exposition des Français au cadmium
france24fr.description: Les Français sont surexposés au cadmium, responsable notamment de l'augmentation des cancers du pancréas. Ce métal lourd est répandu dans les champs par le biais des engrais phosphatés. La concentration maximale autorisée en France est de 90mg de cadmium par kilo d'engrais. L'ANSES préconise un plafond à 20mg seulement. Une proposition de loi a été adoptée en commission à l'Assemblée Nationale. Elle vise à réduire drastiquement les concentrations autorisées.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : même sans Sonko, le président Diomaye Faye a des chances de gouverner sans blocages
france24fr.description: Le président sénégalais, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a fait, lundi, un pas supplémentaire vers la rupture avec son ex-Premier ministre Ousmane Sonko en formant, sans son assentiment pour une particpation du Pastef, un nouveau gouvernement. Selon les analystes, l'exécutif pourrait toutefois fonctionner sans subir de blocage décisif de son ex-allié.

france24fr.title: Cancer du pancréas : le daraxonrasib, un espoir pour retarder la progression de la maladie
france24fr.description: Présenté au congrès international d'oncologie de Chicago, un nouveau traitement contre le cancer du pancréas, le daraxonrasib, a été accueilli comme "un progrès majeur". Pour cause, cet anticancéreux pourrait doubler l'espérance de vie de certains patients et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour le traitement d'autres cancers. Explications.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump assistera au dîner des correspondants de la Maison Blanche reprogrammé en juillet
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump sera bien présent au dîner des correspondants de la Maison Blanche, reprogrammé au 24 juillet après la fusillade qui avait éclaté fin avril. Cette fois, le gala sera "plus intime" et le dispositif sera "nettement renforcé".

france24fr.title: Guerre hybride : l'atout de Poutine ?
france24fr.description: En Ukraine, la guerre se poursuit. La Russie multiplie ses offensives et a mené, la nuit dernière, une attaque de drones contre le territoire ukrainien. Parallèlement, le pétrolier russe Tagor, en provenance de Mourmansk et arraisonné par la Marine nationale ce week-end, est arrivé ce matin en baie de Douarnenez. Dans le même temps, à l’est de l’Europe, un drone russe chargé d’explosifs a pénétré l’espace aérien roumain avant de s’écraser sur un immeuble, faisant deux blessés.

spiegel.description: Der anfängliche Widerstand aus der Techbranche ist offenbar beigelegt: Präsident Donald Trump will US-Behörden bedeutende KI-Zugänge verschaffen. Das hat auch mit einem neuen Hackingwerkzeug zu tun.

spiegel.title: Ehegattensplitting: Wirtschaftsexperten fordern von der Bundesregierung Obergrenze
spiegel.description: In einem offenen Brief an Kanzler Merz und Vizekanzler Klingbeil schlagen namhafte Wirtschaftsforschende eine Reform des Ehegattensplittings vor: Weil sich Mehrarbeit oft kaum lohnt, soll der Steuervorteil gedeckelt werden.

spiegel.title: Libanon: Israel gelingt symbolischer Sieg an Kreuzfahrerburg Beaufort
spiegel.description: Zum zweiten Mal nach 44 Jahren hat Israels Armee die Kreuzfahrerburg Beaufort im Südlibanon eingenommen, die Hisbollah reagiert mit tödlichen Drohnenattacken. Der Ort droht erneut zum Sinnbild eines endlosen Krieges zu werden.

spiegel.title: Polen plant Handyverbot an Grundschulen
spiegel.description: Zum kommenden Schuljahr will Polen Handys aus Grundschulen verbannen. Die Regierung in Warschau hat dafür einen Gesetzentwurf auf den Weg gebracht – auch auf Wunsch vieler Lehrkräfte.

spiegel.title: Stanley Cup und Pokémon: Die Sammelleidenschaft der Vegas Golden Knights
spiegel.description: Das Eishockeyteam Vegas Golden Knights steht im Finale des Stanley Cups. Sollte ihnen der Gewinn der Meisterschaft gelingen, hat das eventuell auch ein bisschen mit Pikachu, Schiggy und Glurak zu tun.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Polizisten legten Sterbendem Handschellen an – Video löst Rassismusdebatte aus
spiegel.description: Ein 23-Jähriger aus der Sikh-Gemeinschaft sticht auf einen 18-Jährigen ein. Als die Polizei eintrifft, hält sie aber zunächst den verletzten Teenager für den Täter. Bodycamaufnahmen lösen in Großbritannien einen Aufschrei aus.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank: UniCredit steigert Anteil auf über ein Drittel
spiegel.description: Die feindliche Übernahme der Commerzbank durch die UniCredit schreitet voran. Die Italiener bauen ihren Anteil auf mehr als 34 Prozent aus und überschreiten damit die wichtige 30-Prozent-Schwelle.

spiegel.title: Radikale Islamisten: »Dschihadisten«, die zu allem entschlossen sind - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Sie haben Hass auf die freie westliche Welt. Das Bundeskriminalamt nennt sie »Gefährder«. Mahmoud Mhemed gehörte für die Beamten nicht dazu. Sein Anschlag auf einen Nachtclub in Bielefeld kam fast aus dem Nichts.

spiegel.title: Serena Williams spielt wieder Tennis: Das Wiederkommen ist so viel leichter als das Aufhören
spiegel.description: Nach vierjähriger Pause kehrt Serena Williams ins Profitennis zurück, mit nunmehr 44 Jahren – an der Seite einer 19-jährigen Doppelpartnerin. Warum macht sie das?

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Warum der Fußball schon an den Namen erkennbar ist
spiegel.description: Zico, Garrincha, Tostão: Früher waren Brasiliens Spitznamen ein Versprechen. Heute klingt die Seleção austauschbar. Schuld daran: Vermarktung, Agentenlogik, der Zeitgeist.

spiegel.title: Alexander Zverev: Wie der Tennisstar zur Antithese der French Open wird
spiegel.description: Während Roland Garros in Favoritenstürzen und Fünfsatzmatches versinkt, lässt sich Alexander Zverev nicht aus der Ruhe bringen. Auch nicht vom 19-jährigen Rafael Jódar und einer besonderen Geräuschkulisse.

spiegel.title: Rheinmetall: Rumänien bestellt Waffen und Munition im Wert von 5,7 Milliarden Euro
spiegel.description: Rheinmetall hat nach eigenen Angaben den größten internationalen Auftrag der jüngeren Unternehmensgeschichte angenommen. Darunter: Panzer, Munition und Schiffe.

spiegel.title: Rostock – Fall Fabian: Angeklagte wendet Blick von grausamen Tatortfotos ab
spiegel.description: Ein Feldweg, hohes Gebüsch, dahinter der leblose Körper: Im Prozess um den gewaltsamen Tod des achtjährigen Fabian geht es um grausame Fotos vom Tatort. Die Verteidigung gibt sich gelassen.

spiegel.title: Yad Vashem in Deutschland: Streit um Einflussnahme und deutsche Erinnerungslücken – ein Debattenbeitrag von Deborah Hartmann
spiegel.description: Deutschland bekommt zwei Außenstellen von Yad Vashem. Nach der Entscheidung warnen Kritiker vor israelischer Einflussnahme. Dabei zeigt ausgerechnet der Protest, wie groß die Leerstellen im deutschen Holocaustgedenken sind.

spiegel.title: Uno-Generalversammlung: Khalilur Rahman übernimmt von Annalena Baerbock »einen der besten Jobs der Welt«
spiegel.description: Ab September wird Khalilur Rahman neuer Präsident der Uno-Vollversammlung und folgt auf Annalena Baerbock. Der früheren Außenministerin attestieren Experten in ihrer Amtszeit eine »zupackende Führungspersönlichkeit«.

observador.title: A caderneta do Mundial como espelho nacional
observador.description: Raramente questionamos mecanismos de consumo que se tornam quase invisíveis quando são acompanhados pela nostalgia.

observador.title: A 1.ª República e esta
observador.description: A existência da 1.ª República encontra-se cheia de perturbadoras similitudes com esta a que António José Seguro preside.

observador.title: Uma novela chamada reforma laboral
observador.description: Esta reforma não deve ser encarada como uma guerra de trincheiras ideológicas, mas sim como uma oportunidade para aproximar a lei da vida real das nossas empresas e dos nossos trabalhadores.

observador.title: Assédio laboral na Enfermagem: o SNS não pode mais ignorar
observador.description: Quando faltam profissionais, aumenta a pressão sobre as equipas e sobre quem gere os serviços. Criam-se ambientes de tensão permanente, desgaste psicológico e conflito.

observador.title: Porque é preciso contar histórias sobre a deficiência?
observador.description: Não se tratará (somente) de uma questão de ética, mas sim do poderoso papel que o storytelling tem ao contar histórias disruptivas, reais, fortes, duras, impactantes, simplesmente diferentes.

observador.title: FSD da Testa legal em mais 2 países europeus. 4º a caminho
observador.description: A Tesla continua a expansão do FSD Supervised na Europa. Homologado para circular sem intervenção humana nos Países Baixos, o FSD foi aprovado na Lituânia e na Estónia, com a Grécia a preparar-se.

observador.title: Quais são as consequências da suspensão da pena de Salgado?
observador.description: Tribunal fixou pena de 13 anos pelas condenações no caso EDP e na Operação Marquês, mas suspendeu execução, lançando a dúvida sobre o que pode suceder nos outros casos. Defesa pondera queixa no TEDH.

observador.title: 23h. Ventura diz ter solução para baixar idade da reforma
observador.description: O presidente do Chega diz que a proposta vai custar 1,8 mil milhões de euros. Ainda, o ministro da presidência acredita que a taxa de desemprego nos jovens é elevada devido à lei laboral atual.

observador.title: Governo prepara reforço da proteção do lobo
observador.description: Ministra do Ambiente promete decreto-lei que irá "proteger ainda mais" o lobo-ibérico, em resposta às críticas face às alterações do PEPAC.

observador.title: Homem de 78 anos morre enquanto pescava em Sesimbra
observador.description: O homem foi encontrado morto ao final da tarde, por uma pessoa que passava no local, numa zona de lodo do interior da lagoa de Albufeira. As causas da morte ainda estão por determinar.

observador.title: Lula critica taxas dos EUA e vai procurar novos mercados
observador.description: Os EUA concluíram que as práticas no Brasil ligadas ao desmatamento ilegal, à pirataria, a falhas na aplicação de leis anticorrupção e ao mercado de etanol prejudicam o comércio norte-americano.

observador.title: Hamilton e Leclerc apertam com o Luce. Acções descem e sobem
observador.description: A Ferrari revelou o Luce, o seu primeiro veículo eléctrico, apresentação que se viu envolvida em polémica. Louvores houve poucos, as críticas abundaram e as acções desceram. Depois, subiram…

observador.title: Acampamento mais alto do Evereste acumula toneladas de lixo
observador.description: Tendas antigas, embalagens de alimentos, garrafas de oxigénio, sacos de transporte e recipientes de gás são alguns dos resíduos encontrados no Everest. Alguns dos detritos remontam a 1957.

observador.title: Vítima de Epstein acusa Buckingham de "proteger" André
observador.description: Jess Michaels afirmou sentir-se feliz por Reino Unido "estar finalmente a investigar" ex-príncipe. Mencionou nome de Virginia Giuffre, vítima de Epstein que afirmou ter sido traficada por André.

observador.title: Trump nomeia aliado como novo diretor dos Serviços Secretos
observador.description: Pulte tem sido responsável por lançar investigações contra democratas, vistos como adversários de Trump, acusando-os de fraude imobiliária. Nenhum deles foi formalmente acusado pela justiça.

observador.title: Mulheres sepultadas com armas há 3.500 anos em Serpa
observador.description: Investigação a 57 sepulturas de há 3.500 anos encontrou mais bens depositados junto a mulheres do que a homens e verificou que o enterro com armas não era um exclusivo masculino.

observador.title: Explicador. Tudo o que precisa de saber sobre o El Niño
observador.description: Depois do El Niño de 2023, que contribuiu para temperaturas recorde em 2024, a Organização Mundial de Meteorologia alerta que o fenómeno poderá repetir ou agravar esse cenário a nível global em 2026.

observador.title: Brad Pitt processado por marca de cremes íntimos
observador.description: O rebranding de Le Domaine para Beau Domaine, em julho de 2025, gerou a disputa judicial. Agora a Beau D., marca de beleza íntima masculina, acusa-a de violação de marca registada e pede 65 mil euros.

elpais.title: Feijóo, sobre ir a Waterloo a negociar con Puigdemont la moción de censura: “Hablemos de cosas serias”
elpais.description: “Devolveré la decencia a mi país con ayuda o sin ella”, asegura el líder del PP en su intervención en el Círculo de Economía

elpais.title: El PSOE eleva ahora de 15.000 a casi 45.000 euros el importe que pagó a Leire Díez por labores de comunicación
elpais.description: El partido detalla los pagos a la exmilitante por su trabajo en Cantabria hace casi una década en un escrito al juzgado de Madrid que investiga una causa distinta a la que llevó a la Audiencia Nacional a enviar a la UCO a Ferraz

elpais.title: Una candidata al puesto de David Sánchez denuncia irregularidades, pero una docena de funcionarios defienden la legalidad del proceso
elpais.description: Cristina de Frutos insiste en el juicio en sus sospechas sobre la adjudicación y la Fiscalía y las defensas cuestionan su testimonio

elpais.title: La princesa Leonor, primera paracaidista de la Familia Real
elpais.description: Zarzuela difunde imágenes de la heredera preparándose para saltar en Alcantarilla (Murcia) como parte de su formación militar

elpais.title: Jódar sucumbe a la majestuosidad de Zverev en Roland Garros
elpais.description: El alemán ofrece un recital, tras un primer set muy debatido, y accede por quinta vez a las semifinales en las seis últimas ediciones: 7-6(3), 6-1 y 6-3, tras 2h 25m

elpais.title: “Han ido a pillar”: casi toda España se suma a la PAU en una Selectividad blindada con detectores de frecuencia
elpais.description: La adolescencia, Manuel Vicent, Emilia Pardo Bazán y la invasión musulmana de la Península, en las preguntas de los ejercicios

elpais.title: Presunta imparcialidad
elpais.description: El doble rasero judicial y policial acaba erosionando la legitimidad de un poder fundamental del Estado

elpais.title: Las reinas no fuman
elpais.description: El mensaje general de doña Letizia casi parecía dirigido a alguien en particular

elpais.title: Bruselas cede y se abre a relajar las reglas de gasto público para que los Estados afronten la crisis energética
elpais.description: La Comisión plantea que los Gobiernos puedan destinar hasta un 0,3% del PIB anual para reducir la dependencia de los combustibles fósiles

elpais.title: Petro insiste en cuestionar las elecciones: “Presento las bases comprobadas del posible fraude”
elpais.description: El presidente colombiano señala un aumento de mesas y cédulas en uno de los varios ‘softwares’ electorales

elpais.title: Putin anuncia una “nueva dimensión” en la guerra contra Ucrania y lanza un intenso ataque que mata al menos a 23 personas
elpais.description: La ofensiva del Kremlin, una de las peores de los últimos meses, golpea Kiev, Dnipró y Járkov y causa un centenar de heridos

elpais.title: Israel y Hezbolá mantienen el fuego cruzado pese al anuncio de Trump del fin de las hostilidades en Líbano
elpais.description: Netanyahu sale escaldado de su plan de bombardear Beirut. Según el medio digital ‘Axios’, el presidente de Estados Unidos lo abroncó por teléfono: “Eres un puto loco”

elpais.title: Marco Rubio sobre la crisis con Cuba: “Hemos hablado con ellos y les hemos dicho lo que tienen que hacer para recuperar su economía”
elpais.description: El secretario de Estado acusa a las autoridades cubanas de patrocinar el terrorismo y de trabajar para el espionaje chino y ruso

elpais.title: El Papa nombra jefa de comunicación del Vaticano a la presidenta de una televisión ultraconservadora de EE UU, hostil a Francisco
elpais.description: María Montserrat Alvarado, de origen mexicano, es la primera mujer laica en un cargo tan alto en la Santa Sede. El pontífice argentino llegó a definir como “obra del diablo” los ataques de la cadena EWTN

elpais.title: Cerca de 400 efectivos luchan contra un incendio en el municipio de Murcia que fuerza el desalojo de unas 100 personas
elpais.description: El fuego, declarado en la pedanía murciana de Garres y Lages, avanza hacia una zona de montaña del parque regional El Valle-Carrascoy

elpais.title: Los vecinos de Retiro se vuelcan con Maricarmen, de 87 años: “Nos encontramos de la noche a la mañana en la calle”
elpais.description: Cientos de personas se manifiestan contra los grandes tenedores en una concentración convocada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid

elpais.title: La inminente llegada de ‘El Niño’ echará “más leña al fuego de un mundo que se calienta”
elpais.description: La Organización Meteorológica Mundial insta a estar preparados ante el riesgo de aumento de los fenómenos extremos alimentados por este evento natural

elpais.title: Illa y Rueda chocan en público por la financiación autonómica: “No hay que jugar a las bilateralidades”
elpais.description: El ‘president’ advierte en el Cercle d’Economia que un Gobierno que dependa de Vox implicará una involución territorial

nyt.title: Order Shielding Trump Family From I.R.S. Audits Will Remain, Blanche Says
nyt.description: The acting attorney general said the administration was preserving a broad order shielding the president and his family from audits of already filed returns, despite dropping a $1.8 billion payout fund.

nyt.title: Trump’s $1.8 Billion Fund Is ‘Not Moving Forward’
nyt.description: Also, California votes on its next governor. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.

nyt.title: Polls of California Governor’s Race Show a Clear Top 3
nyt.description: Xavier Becerra, Steve Hilton and Tom Steyer have consistently led the field in California’s nonpartisan primary, where the top two finishers advance.

nyt.title: Why We Might Not Know California’s Election Results for Days
nyt.description: Polls will close at 8 p.m. local time, but California’s meticulous review process and heavy reliance on mail ballots mean races may not be called quickly.

nyt.title: New Proposal Would Allow Administration to Block Grants if They Don’t Support Trump’s Agenda
nyt.description: A new proposal would allow the administration to block grants if they do not satisfy President Trump’s agenda or support what it calls “anti-American” values.

nyt.title: Trump Names Bill Pulte as Acting Director of National Intelligence
nyt.description: Bill Pulte, a Trump loyalist who leads the federal housing finance agency, will oversee the U.S. intelligence agencies. He has no known background in intelligence.

nyt.title: Trump Signs Executive Order Seeking Oversight of A.I. Models
nyt.description: The order, which signaled a shift from the hands-off approach the White House had previously taken toward A.I., followed debates over how to gain control of A.I. models without disrupting innovation.

nyt.title: Only the Right Tests Can Stop This Ebola Outbreak. Congo Has Hardly Any.
nyt.description: A chronic lack of investment in development of better tests has left clinicians blind and allows deadly viruses to spread unchecked.

nyt.title: U.S. Ebola Unit Plans in Kenya, Subject of Protests, Suffers New Setback From Court Ruling
nyt.description: The court further delayed the Trump administration’s proposed quarantine unit for Americans exposed to the virus. The plan has sparked angry protests in Kenya.

nyt.title: How Three Chess Friends Battled Demons and Saved Two Lives
nyt.description: A homeless chess hustler, a scholar and an aging recluse found hope in a trashed apartment by Central Park.

nyt.title: The Toll of a ‘Missing Scientists’ Conspiracy Theory on the Families Left Behind
nyt.description: The claim that their loved ones’ deaths and disappearances are linked is almost certainly false — but the loss remains real.

nyt.title: Obama Center’s Two Sides: A Lovely Park and a Forbidding Tower
nyt.description: In Chicago, the $850 million Obama Presidential Center aims to remake a neighborhood with a 19.3-acre community hub and a brooding 225-foot museum.

nyt.title: What Ireland and Germany Can Teach Us About Birthright Citizenship
nyt.description: President Trump has argued that the United States is “stupid” for granting citizenship at birth. Most countries don’t do so, but that can create problems.

nyt.title: Carney Says Canada Faces a ‘Crisis of Antisemitism’
nyt.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s comments followed calls for action from Jewish organizations and after a government report found that antisemitism had surged in Canada in recent years.

nyt.title: ‘La La Land’ Orchestral Performance Saved by Keyboardist in the Audience
nyt.description: After a musician fell ill during a live performance of the score from “La La Land,” the composer Justin Hurwitz asked for a sight reader. A 21-year-old student stepped up.

nyt.title: U.S. Treasury Imposes Sanctions on Iran’s Biggest Crypto Exchange
nyt.description: The action against Nobitex and several of its executives accused it of helping the government evade sanctions and finance militants.

nyt.title: In Her Memoir, Jill Biden Is a Watchful Spouse Who Didn’t Always Speak Up About Joe Biden
nyt.description: The former first lady’s new book reflects an insular White House where loyalty was prized and President Joseph R. Biden Jr.’s feelings were prioritized over health concerns.

nyt.title: Book Review: ‘View From the East Wing,’ by Jill Biden
nyt.description: Beyond a few pointed digs at her husband’s successor, “View From the East Wing” largely sticks to the head-spinning details of first lady-hood.

republika.title: Guerra Ucraina-Russia, le news del 2 giugno. Kiev annuncia l’evacuazione di villaggi nella regione di Kharkiv
republika.description: Media: “Almeno 21 morti nei raid russi”. Palazzi in fiamme a Kiev. Ft: “Gli Usa stanno discutendo l’idea di armi nucleari in altri Paesi Nato”

republika.title: Guerra in Iran, le news. Trump: “Falso che abbiamo smesso di parlare. È ora di un accordo”
republika.description: Rubio: “Trattiamo, accordo possibile oggi, domani o la prossima settimana”. Tajani: “La pace? Sono gli Usa che devono fermare Israele”. Raid di Israele in Libano: almeno otto morti, tre sono bambini. Bozza del summit Ue: “Lavorare sulle sanzioni ai ministri estremisti di Israele”. Nave Msc colpita dai pasdaran in un porto iracheno

republika.title: Cortellesi e le partigiane, la memoria che commuove la piazza della Repubblica
republika.description: Cantanti e attori sul palco voluto dal presidente Mattarella per l’evento davanti a 2700 ospiti

republika.title: Omicidio a Roma dopo una lite per i rifiuti: a 18 anni uccide il vicino 57enne
republika.description: Tutto è iniziato poco dopo le 21 in un condominio di via Villastellone, in zona Casal del Marmo alla periferia Ovest di Roma

republika.title: 2 giugno, 80 anni della Repubblica. La parata ai Fori, Mattarella: “Costituzione nostra casa comune”
republika.description: La cerimonia al Milite Ignoto con il capo dello Stato, Crosetto, Meloni. Poi la sfilata ai Fori imperiali fino all’evento speciale in piazza del Quirinale

republika.title: Voto alle donne, la lunga marcia da un diritto all’altro
republika.description: A ottant’anni dalla conquista del suffragio universale, è ora che le figure femminili che oggi comandano si carichino l’onere politico e sociale di agevolare una sempre più diffusa parità di genere nelle professioni, nei salari e nelle relazioni tra i sessi

republika.title: L’orgoglio ucraino di Kostyuk. Bolelli-Vavassori e lo spirito di squadra italico
republika.description: Al Roland Garros emozionano le parole di Marta dopo la vittoria contro la connazionale Svitolina. Il doppio azzurro in semifinale

republika.title: Silvana Sciarra: “Le donne hanno dato molto alla Repubblica, ora devono avere maggiore visibilità”
republika.description: La ex presidente della Consulta, prima giudice costituzionale eletta dal Parlamento, individua nella Carta lo strumento attraverso il quale le cittadine possono vedere valorizzate le proprie competenze

republika.title: Caso Boccia, il legale di Sangiuliano sulla ferita in testa: “Non chiederemo il tentato omicidio”
republika.description: L’avvocato Silverio Sica fa sapere che non esiste nessuna iniziativa in questa direzione e, soprattutto, nessun elemento che, allo stato, consentirebbe di sostenere una simile ipotesi accusatoria

republika.title: Nessy Guerra, l’ex marito va dal viceconsole italiano e lo minaccia: “Ti faccio sparare alle gambe”
republika.description: Tamer Hamouda, che ha denunciato e fatto condannare per adulterio la 26enne sanremese bloccata in Egitto con la figlia, ha chiesto soldi al funzionario: “Sennò finisci su una sedia a rotelle”. La donna: “Ora non siamo solo noi quelli minacciati”

republika.title: Il 2 giugno di Mattarella: “Felici di essere il frutto di tante migrazioni”
republika.description: Il capo dello Stato dialoga con i giovani: no uomini soli al comando, l’allarme per gli affaristi della IA. “Fermare il ritorno della barbarie”

republika.title: Strage dei braccianti, il monito della Cei: “Basta con il silenzio sporco delle convenienze"
republika.description: Vannacci invoca la remigrazione, il governo chiede si faccia piena luce sul dramma di Amendolara. Il Pd: “ Ecco cosa significa essere un invisibile nelle campagne del Sud”

republika.title: Zerocalcare e le polemiche su “Due spicci”: “Problemi? Potevano contattarmi, io sono un alleato”
republika.description: L’artista replica, con un video, alle accuse sulle condizioni di lavoro degli animatori coinvolti nella sua nuova serie animata e attacca Gasparri: “Fa il giustiziere e poi vota contro il salario minimo”

republika.title: Zverev, continua la caccia al primo Slam: battuto Jodar, semifinale al Roland Garros contro Mensik
republika.description: Il tedesco, grande favorito dopo l’uscita di Sinner, mette fine alla corsa del giovane spagnolo. Il ceco batte Fonseca. Bolelli e Vavassori avanti nel doppio

republika.title: Nuova gaffe di Tajani: “Conte e Schlein assenti al 2 giugno”. Ma il cerimoniale non prevede i leader
republika.description: Il vicepremier, parlando del forfait di Salvini, ha commentato che mancavano anche il presidente del Movimento 5 stelle e la leader del Pd

republika.title: Amendolara, c’è un bracciante sopravvissuto: “Ci davano casa e da mangiare ma non i soldi”
republika.description: Il racconto del cittadino afghano rimasto ferito: “Hanno buttato la benzina e poi hanno dato fuoco all’auto. Io sono fuggito dal portellone lasciato aperto”

republika.title: Bad Bunny, la “casita” vip del tour mondiale finisce in tribunale
republika.description: Tanti gli ospiti sul palco che l’hanno visitata: da Chiara Ferragni ad Ana de Armas. Il simbolo dei concerti dell’artista, però, finisce al centro di una causa milionaria

republika.title: Parata 2 giugno, fermati sei ambientalisti: preparavano un blitz all’Altare della Patria
republika.description: Gli attivisti di Extinction Rebellion fermati dalla polizia vicino al cantiere della metro con uno striscione di grandi dimensioni e fumogeni. Denunciati per invasione di terreni ed edifici, tre anche per resistenza

npr.title: Scenes from the aftermath of Russia's latest massive attack on Kyiv
npr.description: Russian missile and drone attacks killed  civilians across Ukraine overnight, in one of Moscow's largest assaults in recent months.

npr.title: EU strikes migration deal for more deportations and detention centers abroad
npr.description: The European Union has moved forward with an overhaul of its migration policy, aiming to ramp up deportations and build detention centers abroad. Critics compared the regulation to the immigration strategy of the Trump administration.

npr.title: Global conflicts push Sri Lanka's economy to the brink
npr.description: Sri Lanka was careening from crisis to crisis, then came the Mideast war. People say they've got no buffer left.

npr.title: Ultra-Orthodox protesters block roads and trains across Israel over military draft
npr.description: Tens of thousands of ultra-Orthodox demonstrated across Israel on Monday, blocking roads and trains and setting cars on fire to protest mandatory enlistment in Israel's military.

npr.title: What to know about U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boats
npr.description: The U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boats have killed over 200 people. The attacks began in September and aim to stem drug flow, but critics question their legality and effectiveness.

npr.title: Russian attack on Ukraine kills 22 people, officials say, as Moscow escalates fighting

new-sci.description: Embryo organoids made from stem cells are enabling scientists to recreate early pregnancy in the lab, unlocking treatments for infertility, miscarriage and pre-eclampsia

phys-org.title: City birds dazzle females with 'borrowed' human items
phys-org.description: Bowerbirds in an Australian city use a range of human items—from glass and plastic to banknotes and even a pair of handcuffs—to impress females, shows new research in Royal Society Open Science. Male bowerbirds create an intricate tunnel of twigs called a bower, then gather colorful items to show to any females that visit.

phys-org.title: Forest resident birds avoid intensive clearcuts, acoustic monitoring shows
phys-org.description: New research reveals that resident forest birds avoid intensive clearcut areas, highlighting the need for more sustainable forestry practices.

phys-org.title: Laser beam builds cell-like protein networks without chemical modification
phys-org.description: Networks of protein fibers play important roles in living cells. To understand the dynamical behavior of these networks, model networks are needed to perform in vitro studies. However, fabrication of protein networks similar to those in cells has proved difficult, as current methods could affect the biological function of these proteins—ultimately impacting our understanding of any findings.

phys-org.title: Conifers are making a comeback in Quebec's forests, study shows
phys-org.description: An analysis of Quebec's forest inventory data developed by Concordia researchers reveals that the conifer population is on the rebound after decades of decline.

phys-org.title: Canadian forest fires are losing their climate cooling power, says study
phys-org.description: Diminishing periods of snow cover in northern forests, shortened by climate change, are poised to disrupt a delicate balance in some of the planet's most climate-sensitive regions—according to new research from McMaster University, VU Amsterdam, and the Woodwell Climate Research Center.

phys-org.title: Ceres' surface is much more complex than previously thought
phys-org.description: The long, puzzling dwarf planet Ceres, in reality the first named asteroid, has surface features that are much more complex than previously thought. Or at least that's the conclusion of a recent paper presented at the European Geosciences Union 2026 General Assembly in Vienna.

phys-org.title: Small Magellanic Cloud is being pulled apart, reshaping how astronomers read its past
phys-org.description: Using more than a decade of observations from the VISTA Survey of the Magellanic Clouds (VMC), researchers measured the motions of millions of stars across the Small Magellanic Cloud with unprecedented precision. The new study, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, provides direct evidence of a galaxy-wide tidal disruption of the Small Magellanic Cloud from its interaction with the Large Magellanic Cloud.

phys-org.title: Tiny nest box change could help rare pygmy-possums after bushfires
phys-org.description: A 1-millimeter difference in the size of a nest box entrance could help rare little pygmy-possums recover after bushfire, according to new research by Adelaide University, Kangaroo Island Research Station, and Kangaroo Island Dance School.

phys-org.title: Nine decades of changing insect diversity in Switzerland expose a striking divide
phys-org.description: Thanks to a historical data archive, Swiss researchers are able to draw conclusions about the changes in the diversity of two insect groups over the past 90 years. The study, led by Agroscope, identified a significant decline in butterflies and deadwood beetle species around the middle of the 20th century. These groups live predominantly in agricultural and forest habitats. However, the study also shows that the number of species has since risen in some areas.

phys-org.title: Q&A: How better climate data supports smarter environmental decisions
phys-org.description: Accurate measurements are the foundation of effective environmental management and decision-making. Through advanced monitoring networks and computer models, Ken Davis, professor of meteorology and atmospheric science in Penn State's College of Earth and Mineral Sciences, and his research group are helping scientists, communities, and policymakers better understand urban heat, greenhouse gas emissions, and air quality.

phys-org.title: Faster lower-cost PFAS testing could reshape how US drinking water is monitored
phys-org.description: A new investigation from the University of Kansas improves detection of PFAS, a family of so-called "forever chemicals" in drinking water supplies. The method, which can measure trace pollution levels of PFAS in water more quickly and inexpensively than current techniques, was recently detailed in the journal PLOS Water.

phys-org.title: Atmospheric rivers over Japan intensify 8% in 42 years, raising flood risk
phys-org.description: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are long, narrow bands of intense water vapor transport that move large amounts of moisture from low to midlatitudes, resembling giant rivers in the sky. They are gaining widespread attention because of their potential to trigger flooding across the Japanese archipelago. Researchers at the University of Tsukuba have discovered that, influenced by global warming and the strengthening of the North Pacific Subtropical High, the intensity of water vapor transport in ARs has

phys-org.title: Antarctic 'sky rivers' deliver up to 90% of snowfall, 3D algorithm suggests
phys-org.description: Atmospheric rivers act like "rivers in the sky," shuttling intense bands of warm, heavy moisture from lower to higher latitudes. When an atmospheric river encounters cold air or mountainous terrain, the moisture it carries condenses and falls as heavy rain or snow. In Antarctica, the arrival of an atmospheric river can help build surface ice mass. Much of Antarctica is very dry; an atmospheric river can bring the moisture needed to potentially offset some ice loss.

phys-org.title: Bees can swim and use visual cues to survive water crashes
phys-org.description: When a bee crashes into water, it may still be able to swim to safety. New research from Michigan State University confirms that honeybees can propel themselves across the water's surface, and their movement is purposeful and directional. They swim toward darker areas—likely using visual cues to locate the shoreline and escape. This study was recently published in Communications Biology.

phys-org.title: Connected boards echo climate rules, yet many firms move pollution instead
phys-org.description: The good news: When environmental rules pressure one company, the effect can spread through shared boardroom ties, leading connected firms to reduce emissions, too.

phys-org.title: Proteins can be selectively controlled with radio waves
phys-org.description: In a significant advance in biological quantum sensing, a research team led by the Technical University of Munich (TUM) has discovered and tested a new mechanism of action in which proteins can be controlled with radio waves. In doing so, they influence a sensitive quantum state known as spin and make it visible via light. In the future, such findings could help detect and even direct biochemical processes in cells simply from the outside using radio waves.

phys-org.title: Environmental engineers reshape understanding of airborne pollution particles
phys-org.description: From sizzling bacon in the kitchen to wildfire smoke in the sky, cooking and pollution release microscopic particles that affect humans' health, the air they breathe, and even weather and climate. New research from Virginia Tech is poised to upend how scientists think about the structure of these tiny airborne droplets and what that means for predictions around air quality, pollution spread, and climate models.

phys-org.title: Municipal partnership systems and mental health among sexual minorities in Japan: A nationwide analysis
phys-org.description: Although same-sex marriage has not been legalized nationally in Japan, various municipal governments have independently introduced partnership certification systems for same-sex couples.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering
proj-syn.description: The productivity growth that transformed agriculture across Latin America and the Caribbean has slowed sharply in recent years, with farmers increasingly relying on costly inputs rather than efficiency gains. Without sustained public investment, the region risks losing competitiveness and reversing decades of hard-won progress.
